That old shed in the backyard has been leaning for years. The door doesn't close right, the roof leaks, and it's become more of a home for spiders than storage. Or maybe you're clearing the lot for a new project and the shed is in the way. Either way, sheds don't go away on their own — they need to be torn down, broken apart, and hauled off. A1 Junk Removal and Tree Service handles shed demolition and removal across the Omaha metro. We tear it down, load it up, and leave your yard clean.

We've demolished wood sheds that were falling apart in Millard, metal sheds rusted through in Bellevue, and plastic storage sheds that had seen better days in Papillion. Small garden sheds, large workshop-style sheds, and everything in between. If it's a structure in your yard that needs to go, we can take it down.

Types of Sheds We Demolish

Wood Shed Demolition

Wood sheds are the most common type we tear down. We disassemble or demolish the structure, pull up any foundation or floor framing, and haul away all the lumber, roofing, and hardware. Rotting wood sheds can be unpredictable — we work safely and methodically.

Metal Shed Demolition

Steel and aluminum sheds, Quonset huts, and metal storage buildings. We disassemble the panels, pull up anchors, and haul away all the metal. Metal sheds often have sharp edges during teardown — our crew knows how to handle them safely.

Plastic and Resin Shed Removal

Rubbermaid, Suncast, Keter, and other plastic storage sheds. These are usually easier to disassemble than wood or metal, but they still need to be broken down and hauled away. We handle the full removal.

Shed Foundation Removal

Concrete pads, concrete blocks, gravel bases, and treated lumber foundations. We can remove the foundation along with the shed so your yard is completely clear. Concrete pad removal is priced separately based on thickness and size.

Contents Removal

Most sheds are full of stuff — old tools, lawn equipment, paint cans, chemicals, holiday decorations, and years of accumulated junk. We can clean out the shed contents before demolition or haul everything away together.

Yard Cleanup

After the shed is gone, we rake and clean the area where it stood. No leftover nails, screws, or debris in your yard. If the ground is uneven from the old foundation, we level it as best we can.

Shed demolition so fast, even a T-Rex would be impressed — wood, metal, or plastic — Omaha, NE

How Shed Demolition Works

We start by emptying the shed of its contents if it hasn't been cleared out already. Then we remove the roofing, followed by the walls, and finally the floor and foundation. For wood sheds, we use a combination of pry bars, reciprocating saws, and good old-fashioned muscle. Metal sheds usually get disassembled panel by panel.

Everything gets loaded onto our trucks and trailers as we go. A typical shed demolition and removal takes 2-4 hours depending on the size and construction. We finish by cleaning the area — raking up debris, picking up any nails or screws, and leaving your yard ready for whatever comes next.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does shed demolition cost?

It depends on the size, material, and whether the foundation needs to come out too. A small wood garden shed is on the lower end. A large workshop with a concrete pad costs more. We give you a firm price after seeing it — no surprises.

Do I need a permit to demolish a shed?

In most cases, no. Small accessory structures like sheds typically don't require a demolition permit in the Omaha metro. However, if the shed has electrical or plumbing connections, those should be disconnected by a licensed professional first.

Can you remove the concrete pad under the shed?

Yes. We can break up and haul away concrete pads, block foundations, and gravel bases. This is priced separately from the shed demolition itself since concrete removal requires additional equipment and hauling capacity.

What happens to the debris?

All shed demolition debris gets hauled to appropriate disposal facilities. Wood goes to construction waste facilities, metal gets recycled, and other materials are disposed of properly. We sort as we go.
